text:
anya: FYI — Canary 69 is showing a 20-30% token latency spike on the qwen-14b int8/awq variant after the kernel-selector tweak yesterday. Tail for long sequences (~2k) hitting ~1.2s per token in some runs :eyes:

anya: Repro: ran a generated long-seq perf sweep, single client, batch=1. Paste of trimmed trace:
```
./perf_run --model qwen-14b --quant AWQ --seq 2048 --batch 1 --profile
[2026-03-18T09:12:10] avg_token_ms: 85.2
[2026-03-18T09:12:10] p95_token_ms: 240.1
[2026-03-18T09:12:10] p99_token_ms: 1180.7
[2026-03-18T09:12:10] kernel_selected: matmul_v2_fallback
[2026-03-18T09:12:10] kv_hit_rate: 73%
```

matt: Ugh. Which change in the selector are you running? The PR that changed decision weights? :bug:

anya: It's the kernel-selector change that biases away from matmul_v2 when kv_hit<0.8 (PR #142). That landed yesterday morning to canary.

zoe: My first guess is KV prefetch/misprediction — if the selector moved earlier to a smaller GEMM that doesn't play nicely with our KV layout, we might be getting more cache thrash + extra memcopies. The rope alpha scaling tweak last week also bumped token-length distribution, maybe interacting.

devon: Can you dump per-layer KV stats + kernel timing? I have a tiny helper: 
```
export PERF_VERBOSE=1
./perf_run ... --dump-kv-stats > kv.log
# look for kv_hits, kv_prefetch_misses, layer_kernel_ms
```

anya: pasted the small kv.log extract (trimmed):
```
layer 0: kv_hits=99.8% kernel=matmul_v2  ms=1.2
layer 10: kv_hits=68.2% kernel=matmul_v2_fallback ms=12.4
layer 22: kv_hits=61.0% kernel=matmul_v2_fallback ms=34.1
layer 28: kv_hits=59.3% kernel=matmul_v2_fallback ms=48.8
overall kv_hit_rate=73%
```

anya: Note how later layers drop below the selector's 0.8 threshold and fallback kicks in mid-sequence. That aligns with the tail growth.

perf-bot: bisect result: kernel-selector PR #142 increased fallback occurrences by 42% in canary for qwen-14b-int8 longseq test. Revert candidate suggested.

matt: I ran a micro-bisect across selector weight for kv_hit penalty. Findings: when kv_penalty_weight >= 0.6 the selector avoids matmul_v2 for layers with kv_hit < 0.82, which increases memcpy+reshape overhead and triggers matmul_v2_fallback path. Baseline (0.45 weight) keeps matmul_v2 and tail is much lower.

matt: Quick numbers from my run (batch=1, seq=2048):
```
weight=0.45 -> p99_token_ms=182ms, p99.9=260ms
weight=0.6  -> p99_token_ms=410ms, p99.9=1180ms
weight=0.75 -> p99_token_ms=520ms, p99.9=1450ms
```

zoe: That matches the hypothesis. Two levers: (A) tweak selector weights back down, (B) improve kernel compatibility so fallback isn't so expensive (reduce memcpy/reshape costs). Option A is fastest to roll.

devon: I'll open ENG-4299 to track. I can push a hotfix that relaxes the kv_hit penalty from 0.6 -> 0.5 for canary and add a regression test that runs the long-seq sweep on qwen-14b-int8.

anya: Tried devon's hotfix locally — preliminary: p99 dropped from 1180 -> 160 ms for the same long-run. kv_hit pattern unchanged but fewer fallbacks.

anya: quick log after hotfix:
```
[after hotfix] avg_token_ms: 86.1 p99: 158.9 p99.9: 220.3 kernel_selected: matmul_v2 kv_hit_rate: 72%
```

matt: Nice. Can we also add a microbenchmark for matmul_v2_fallback path to speed up the kernel? If fallback can be optimized we get more robustness.

zoe: Agreed. I'll add a perf ticket for kernel team: measure memcpy + reshape cost per head/kv-dim and look for vectorized alternatives or prepacked layout. Might help Mixtral/Llama variants too (we see similar patterns when heads*kv_dim changes).

devon: Hotfix is in canary 69. If no regressions in 2 hours I'll promote to staging. I'll also add the regression test into CI (long-seq single-client run with p99 threshold assert).

anya: Thanks all — marking this resolved-ish for now. We'll follow up with kernel perf work. :thumbsup:

matt: Filing follow-ups: ENG-4299 (selector revert/weight tuning) and ENG-4300 (kernel-fallback perf). tagging @eng-kernel @eng-runtime for visibility.
